screening.usefulness_reason: Useful for generic conceptual mathematics. Recollement expresses an ambient category as compatible stable/acyclic and ordinary-derived pieces, with adjoints producing a functorial decomposition triangle. Compact objects act as a finite or bounded semantic skeleton whose closure under triangles and coproducts reconstructs an unbounded completion. Quotienting by perfect objects forgets regular information and retains singularity, while support localization proves that removing a regular locus preserves the stable category. Complete resolutions and their adjoints turn approximation into a universal property and generate Tate cohomology; orthogonality conditions give complementary approximation classes. The appendices add two broadly reusable representation moves: replace a compactly generated homotopy category by a DG category, and split any injective complex canonically up to isomorphism into a homotopically minimal part plus a null-homotopic part. These mechanisms test decomposition, obstruction/vanishing, canonicality, dual viewpoints, and representation change without relying on concrete arithmetic execution.
